page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.3xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance provisions 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache layout consists of 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. It provides instruction support including AVX, AVX-512F, BMI2, ADX, and AES-NI, though it lacks newer extensions such as AVX-512 VNNI or AMX.

The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of memory, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes without bundled local storage (0 GB), necessitating network-attached storage for persistence. Network connectivity is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps, and no dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate moderate multi-threaded capability balanced against limited single-thread throughput. Single-core tests show constrained performance, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 929.0 and a single-core stress-ng rating of 1107.69, both placing in bottom-tier percentiles. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression yield poor throughput. When fully utilizing all 16 vCPUs, the instance reaches mid-tier performance across multi-threaded workloads, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 5695.0, a PassMark CPU score of 13258.46, and 57.07 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

Memory and application-level benchmarks align with mid-range compute expectations. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 77.43 GB/sec with write speeds at 59.68 GB/sec. Application testing shows 11.29 million Redis SET operations per second, a static web serving throughput of 7.65 GB/sec, and consistent results in Clang software compilation and ray tracing. For lightweight machine learning workloads, prompt processing on a small 135M model sustains 800.66 tokens per second, though larger 7B models exhibit weak performance at 8.13 generation tokens per second.

Qualitatively, the ecs.sn1.3xlarge offers cost-effective parallel compute density for workloads that scale across threads rather than relying on high clock speeds. The primary operational tradeoffs involve modest single-core execution speed and the requirement of external block storage. The instance fits parallel build systems, CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch processing, and horizontally scaled web serving environments.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance is tailored for multi-threaded processing tasks without the provision of local storage or GPU hardware. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 3 Gbps. Benchmark analysis reflects weak single-core processing capabilities, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 929.0, countered by steady mid-range multi-core efficiency, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core result of 5695.0 and 11.29 million Redis SET operations per second. The server offers a balanced compute-to-cost profile for parallel batch jobs, web serving, and CI/CD compilation workflows that do not require high per-thread burst speeds.
